did_you_know.text: Did you know? Proverbs describes a gentle answer as a force that calms anger, while hurtful words can intensify and worsen it.
Did you know? According to the verse, the eyes of the Lord are everywhere, watching both the wicked and the good.
Did you know? The tongue is presented as a tree of life when it brings healing, but deceitful and stubborn speech can break the spirit.

Did you know? The verse teaches that it is not the sacrifice itself that matters, but a person’s moral conduct: the sacrifice of the wicked is detestable, while the prayer of the upright is pleasing to the Lord.
Did you know? Proverbs contrasts the discerning heart that seeks knowledge with the mouth of fools that feeds on folly.
Did you know? A simple meal of vegetables accompanied by love is presented as better than a feast of a fattened ox accompanied by hatred.
Did you know? The verse emphasizes the value of seeking advice: plans may fail without counsel, but with many advisers they can succeed.
Did you know? Alongside condemning the house of the proud, the verse says that the Lord establishes a boundary and protects the widow’s inheritance.
Did you know? The heart of the righteous considers how to answer, unlike the mouth of the wicked, which hastily pours out evil words.
Did you know? The chapter ends by connecting the fear of the Lord with moral wisdom and teaching that humility comes before honor.
